content.text:
I've reproduced the crash live (twice) with a fresh log capture and screen recording. Here's the full report:

## Reproduction Steps
1. Launch **BenchTarget** (`dev.lincforge.benchtarget`) on an Android **phone** (confirmed on both a Samsung/Pixel phone session; the Wear OS companion build on a Pixel Watch 2 has no catalog feature — only a "Ping" screen — so this bug is phone-only).
2. On the home screen, tap **Catalog**.
3. Scroll down the catalog list to **Item 013** (13th item, "early part of the list" as reported).
4. Tap **Item 013** to open its detail screen ("Catalog entry for Item 013.").
5. Tap the **Export** button.
6. → App immediately crashes and drops to the home launcher.

Items 001–012 were individually tested (Export tapped on each) and did **not** crash — the defect is isolated specifically to Item 013.

## Crash Exception
```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: export buffer not initialized
    at dev.lincforge.benchtarget.core.ExportPolicy.export(ExportPolicy.kt:11)
    at dev.lincforge.benchtarget.ui.ScreensKt.DetailScreen$lambda$0$0$0(Screens.kt:90)
    at dev.lincforge.benchtarget.ui.ScreensKt.$r8$lambda$gZSUvVQNwRksedsE-bpwFrlyFRQ(Screens.kt:0)
    ...
```
Logged as `FATAL EXCEPTION: main`, process `dev.lincforge.benchtarget` — uncaught, kills the app.

## Additional Evidence
- **Live reproduction, twice**, each producing an identical crash trace (PID 8392 at 02:46:36 and PID 6841 at 03:56:18 device time) — same exception, same stack, same line (`ExportPolicy.kt:11`).
- **Screen recording** of the crash: `/Users/<REDACTED>/projects/mobile-agent-bench/recording-1783853771005.mp4` (plus gesture telemetry JSON alongside it).
- **Screenshots**: Item 013 detail screen pre-crash, and post-crash showing the app ejected to the home launcher (`com.google.android.apps.nexuslauncher` foregrounded).
- **Full logcat excerpt** saved at `/Users/<REDACTED>/.agent-device/sessions/verify1/app.log`, including the `screen transition: catalog -> detail` and `Exception dispatching input event` lines immediately preceding the fatal crash.
- Earlier systematic sweep marks in the same log (`before-export-item001` … `before-export-item013`) corroborate that items 1–12 export cleanly and only item013 triggers the fault.

**Root cause hint:** the exception message ("export buffer not initialized") combined with it only affecting item 013 suggests `ExportPolicy` has an uninitialized/lazily-initialized buffer that isn't set up for at least this one catalog entry (possibly index-dependent, e.g. an off-by-one or a buffer that's only primed for the first N items).
